traits.petal_apex.note: Of the showy bracts, which the flower card draws as its petals: broad and rounded, often with a small point at the tip, in iNaturalist photographs (Imagekit count trial, 2026-10-19, 91 heads); drawn acute (point 0.6) they read as square-ish. The flower card's point is set to the petal_apex rule's obtuse value (0.25) by hand, as the rule reaches only looks drawn with flower cards, not a seasonal flower look.

traits.limb_angle.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, p. 787): 'small spreading branches forming an oblong conic or ultimately round-topped head'.

traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Cornus nuttallii (read 2026-10-18): the leaves "turn orange to purplish in autumn". Colour ours, between the two.

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 51 records annotated as flowering (Apr 32, May 18, Jun 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, April and May. FEIS (Cornus nuttallii) gives April to June across the range.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Cornus nuttallii): ripe in September and October across the range.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Cornus Nuttallii: grows 4 m to 25 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Cornus Nuttallii: leaves 5 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Cornus nuttallii (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.6 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.61, branches 0.58. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Gucker 2005, read): Pacific dogwood flowers first when about 6 years old; others report a minimum seed-bearing age of 10, as the Woody Plant Seed Manual's table 3 (Cornus, read) does. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 6 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small understory tree with a rounded crown, opposite oval leaves with curving veins, and large white flower heads of four to six petal-like bracts. Not fitted to measurements. Its pipe_tip, pipe_organ and pipe_rings are scaled together (crown calibration, broadleaf revision 9) so that, with the leaf its crown now keeps, its trunk reaches the reference dbh of 20 cm at 40 years again.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 10 m tall at 40 years in a closed stand. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated. The diameter once given with the height was the same kind of guess and is gone: it asked for about 2 cm of trunk per metre of height in a closed stand, where red alder's normal yield tables (Worthington et al. 1960, Tables 1 and 5) give 0.8 to 1.5, and a guessed girth does not gate the size test.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: green leaves; white bracts round a greenish button; smooth grey-brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: tight heads of green drupes that turn red in autumn. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white bracts in April and May; the fruit heads green in summer, red in September and October. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth thin grey-brown bark becoming checkered into small plates; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): a shade-tolerant understory tree: broad thin shade leaves, smaller narrower sun leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.
